chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Shihab, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام:

Regarding a man who freed a servant of his on the eve of Arafah, he عليه السلام said: "The Hajj of Islam suffices for the servant, and two rewards are written for the master: the reward of emancipation and the reward of Hajj."

key_terms.أَجْرَانِ: two rewards granted in this case
key_terms.السَّيِّدِ: the master who freed the slave
key_terms.الْحَجِّ: the pilgrimage, for which reward is also written
key_terms.الْعَبْدِ: the slave or servant whose legal status changes through emancipation
key_terms.الْعِتْقِ: emancipation or manumission of the slave
key_terms.حَجَّةُ الْإِسْلَامِ: the obligatory hajj that fulfills the foundational duty of pilgrimage
key_terms.عَشِيَّةَ عَرَفَةَ: the eve of Arafah, the specific time mentioned for emancipation

ai.seo_question: Does the hajj of a slave freed on the eve of Arafah count as Hajj al-Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a slave who is emancipated on the eve of Arafah and then performs hajj. It states that the hajj counts as the Hajj of Islam for the freed servant, while the former master receives two rewards: one for freeing the slave and one connected to the hajj.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2891 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Shihab, from Abu Abdullah (as), regarding a man who freed his servant on the eve of Arafah.
Imam (as) said: "The Hajj of Islam suffices for the servant, and the master is rewarded twice: once for the act of freeing the servant and once for the reward of the Hajj."
